items.n: Jamestown Fire and EMS Volunteer Department
items.b: Volunteer fire and emergency medical organization providing response, training and prevention outreach. Fire-prevention outreach and training; no dated public winter event confirmed on its public events page.

Jamestown Fitness Center offers gym equipment, personal training and group classes from its Southwest Avenue location. Its Chamber listing notes that classes are available to nonmembers as well as members. That gives visitors and residents an option to inquire about individual classes without assuming a full membership is required.

The fitness center welcomes members and nonmembers to small group strength and dance exercise classes. November 2026: Total Body Tone Wednesdays and Fridays 9:00 AM; Zumba Gold Thursdays 9:30 AM except November 26. Contact the center or attend an advertised class; single-class prices are $8 for members and $12 for nonmembers.

Jamestown Golf Course is a public nine-hole course with a snack bar and lounge. Its own website dates the course to 1901, connecting present-day play with more than a century of golf on the island. The site also posts tournament and league information that may affect access on a particular day.

The town commission conducts public business concerning harbor management. Third Tuesday 5:00 PM; check the posted agenda. Attend a posted public meeting; apply through the town for a vacant commission seat.

Jamestown Hardware supplies everyday repair and household needs, including hardware, paint, plumbing supplies, lawn and garden items, housewares and key services. Its Chamber profile also lists UPS service. The store's broad inventory makes it a practical village resource for small projects that would otherwise require a trip off the island.

items.a: Museum: 92 Narragansett Avenue; mail: PO Box 156
items.b: Jamestown Historical Society preserves and interprets the island's history through its museum and historic sites. Its responsibilities include the 1787 windmill, the 1786 Friends Meetinghouse and the Revolutionary-era Conanicut Battery. The museum on Narragansett Avenue provides a starting point for exploring these connections between the village and the wider island.

Jamestown Kitchen and Bath designs kitchens, bathrooms, mudrooms, laundry areas and other functional living spaces. Its work also includes coffee stations, bar areas and outdoor spaces. The business operates by appointment at its Narragansett Avenue location, allowing projects to begin with a discussion of the client's needs and layout.
nt: By appointment only.

items.b: A former schoolhouse hosts changing exhibitions about island history. 2026 public season ended October 12; appointments available; 2027 schedule unknown. Request a special visit by email; the museum states it is wheelchair accessible.

Jamestown Newport Ferry provides seasonal passenger transportation linking Jamestown with Newport-area stops, including waterfront destinations and attractions. It is part of the Cruise RI operation. The service is useful for a day across the bay, but routes, operating dates and weather-related changes should be checked before travel.

Jamestown Outdoors offers bicycle, kayak and stand-up paddleboard rentals, along with outdoor-related retail items. Founders Jason and Beth Hatch describe a family bicycle trip as part of the inspiration for the business. Rental arrangements can include delivery, so contact the business about equipment, pickup and the intended outing.

Parent and teacher organization supporting Jamestown school activities and family involvement. School-support activities and meetings; an official March 2026 meeting confirms current activity, but no requested-period public meeting schedule was verified.

Town department running community facilities, recreation classes and public cultural activities. Fitness, tai chi, morning stretch and other classes; quarterly blood drives; community arts and holiday events. Teen Center Monday–Friday 2:30–6:00 PM, closed holidays; program registration has the current session details.

Public library providing lending, research help and programs for children, teens and adults. Rusty Pens Monday 10:30 AM; LEGO Monday 3:00 PM; storytime on published Wednesdays/Thursdays 10:15 AM; Needles Galore on listed Mondays 2:00 PM; first-Wednesday knitting/crochet 5:30 PM; Tuesday movies 1:30 PM on posted dates; Drop-In Genealogy usually first Tuesday 5:30 PM, with November’s date changed to November 17; Monday Mysteries fourth Monday 4:00 PM; Brown Bag Book Club fourth Tuesday noon; Dewey’s Readers third Wednesday 4:00 PM. Youth book clubs, Baby Jam, playtime, crafts, concerts and appointment-only tax help have dated calendar entries. Holiday exceptions apply.
Adults play in the town’s registered pickup basketball leagues. Tuesdays 7:00–9:00 PM during advertised sessions. Register and pay for the relevant series in the town’s online recreation portal.

Emilie Tamboe teaches registered group fitness classes. Monday and Thursday mornings; Tuesday and Friday 8:30 and 9:30 AM; consult each session. Register and pay for the relevant series in the town’s online recreation portal.

items.n: Jamestown Recreation Dungeons and Dragons Club
items.b: Fifth- and sixth-graders learn collaborative fantasy role-playing. Mondays 3:45–5:45 PM through November 9, 2026. Register and pay for the relevant series in the town’s online recreation portal.

Young players learn to design and lead tabletop adventures. Fall Tuesdays 3:30–5:30 PM; winter introductory class selected Thursdays 3:30–5:30 PM. Register and pay for the relevant series in the town’s online recreation portal.
Adults gather for a registered guitar-circle series. Selected Wednesdays 6:15–8:15 PM through December 16, 2026. Register and pay for the relevant series in the town’s online recreation portal.
Val Trainor leads a dance exercise class for registered participants. Selected Sundays 8:30–9:15 AM. Register and pay for the relevant series in the town’s online recreation portal.

Registered participants practice stretching with Emilie Tamboe. Wednesdays: fall 8:00 and 9:00 AM; winter and spring 8:30 and 9:30 AM. Register and pay for the relevant series in the town’s online recreation portal.

The town offers pickleball leagues and instruction at several experience levels. Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday leagues plus Monday, Tuesday and Thursday lessons; times vary by session. Register and pay for the relevant series in the town’s online recreation portal.
Shahin Barzin leads tai chi series at advertised ability levels. Selected Wednesdays 5:00 and 6:00 PM. Register and pay for the relevant series in the town’s online recreation portal.

Children participate in grade-based basketball programs. Saturdays January–March 2027; 8:45 AM, 9:55 AM or noon according to grade. Register and pay for the relevant series in the town’s online recreation portal.

Local Rotary service club supporting community projects and fellowship. Second and fourth Thursdays 7:15 AM at Saint Matthew’s parish hall, rear entrance on West Street; first and third Thursday evening meetings have no published time in the district listing.

Town service offering social, educational, fitness and support programs for older adults; temporarily operating at the golf-course clubhouse. Lunch Monday–Friday 11:30 AM–12:30 PM; Zumba Gold Monday 10:00 AM, $5; Craft Circle Tuesday, with conflicting start times of 9:30 AM in the description and 11:00 AM in the calendar; experienced-player mah jongg Tuesday 2:30 PM; Heart Wise Walking description says Monday/Wednesday/Friday 9:00 AM, but only dated calendar occurrences are listed in Part B. Counseling on posted third Wednesdays 1:00–4:30 PM by appointment. Other classes and wellness programs appear in the town calendar.
Neighborhood organization supporting community gatherings and the shores area. Community meetings, summer picnic and holiday gathering; current dates and times not confirmed.
Community organization providing recreational and travel soccer. Fall recreational soccer and spring/fall travel programs; organization only.
Volunteers care for the island’s public trees and tree nursery. Third Wednesday; time unknown. Contact the committee about nursery volunteering or the town’s committee application.

Local branch of The Village Common of Rhode Island connecting older residents with neighbors, activities and practical support. Community coffee gatherings and volunteer activities; individual listings specify which activities are open to visitors.

The historical society preserves an eighteenth-century working windmill. 2026 public season ended October 12; special visits by arrangement; 2027 schedule unknown. Email for an off-season appointment; admission no charge with donations welcome; onsite parking; interior is not wheelchair accessible.

Sailing organization offering racing, cruising and social activities without a permanent clubhouse. Seasonal sailing, cruising and Fools’ Rules Regatta; organization only, with no sports events included in Part B.

An owner-operated business offers furnished island vacation homes. Availability by property and booking dates. Choose a property and inquire through https://www.jamestownrirental.com/our-homes; verify the host’s town and state registration.

items.n: JB’s on the Water event venue
items.b: The waterfront restaurant offers private-event and catering inquiries. By reservation. Use https://jbsonthewater.com/private-events; capacity, rates and winter availability unknown.

The historical society provides access to its local-history collections and displays. Tuesdays and Thursdays 9:00 AM–noon; check holiday exceptions. Visit during posted research hours or email about a collection inquiry.

items.n: Kayak and paddleboard rentals — Jamestown Outdoors
items.b: An island outfitter arranges kayak and paddleboard rentals. By advance reservation; winter availability unknown. Call for kayaks and launching instructions; published SUP rate $65/day or $200/week; paddle and life jacket included; do not assume rentals operate during winter.
An apparel business makes customized clothing and sailing gear. Shop online or contact the business before visiting.
Jamestown middle school presenting student music, arts and learning activities. Band and chorus concerts and school-family events; dates are published on the district calendar.

Parents and community participants work with the school on improvement priorities. November 19, January 21 and March 11, 3:00–4:30 PM. Register your interest using the form linked from the team’s school page.
Children build with the library’s LEGO materials after school. Posted Mondays 3:00–4:00 PM. No registration; recommended ages 5–10, with an adult nearby for children under ten.
Students in grades 5–8 help shape library activities and services. November 4 and December 2, 4:00–4:30 PM. Contact Youth Services or attend the advertised session.
Young children and caregivers explore stories, songs and movement. Posted Wednesdays and Thursdays 10:15–10:45 AM. Register through the event page; ages 0–5 with a caregiver.

Children in grades 1 and 2 read together and complete an activity. First Thursday 3:30–4:15 PM on the posted dates. Visit the Youth Services desk or email the child’s name, grade and any food allergies.
Regional baseball and softball league whose official announcement welcomes Jamestown players. Seasonal youth baseball and softball; organization only, with no games listed.
Local knitters gather to work on their projects. Selected Mondays 2:00–4:00 PM; see dated calendar. Contact the library or consult the event page before attending.

items.n: New England Sailing Center — charters and instruction
items.b: A sailing school offers instruction and bareboat or captained yacht charters. Jamestown charter prices are listed for June–October; November–March local availability unknown. Contact the center and submit its sailing-resume form for bareboat eligibility; J/22 listings quote $150 half-day or $250 full-day, subject to availability.
nt: Hours and details not recently confirmed; check before visiting.

items.b: Jamestown visitors can reach Newport by road, bus or seasonal ferry. Route 64 timetable; seasonal ferry; no verified regular winter ferry. Use Route 64’s current timetable or drive across the Pell Bridge; check ferry season before planning a water connection.

Older young readers discuss chapter books with library staff. First Wednesday 3:15–4:00 PM on the posted dates. Sign up at the Youth Services desk, borrow the book and read as much as possible before the meeting.

The library lists a book club under the Page to Plate name. December 16 and January 27 at 4:00 PM; other dates unknown. Ask the library for participation details; the published description is incomplete.

Monday–Wednesday 9:00 AM–8:00 PM; Thursday–Saturday 9:00 AM–5:00 PM on the dedicated hours page; holiday exceptions apply. Visit during library hours for no-charge internet access; outdoor or after-hours signal access unknown.
Volunteer garden club caring for civic plantings and supporting gardening education. Seasonal plant sale and volunteer gardening projects; no dated winter schedule confirmed.

The town rents a pavilion for gatherings at Fort Getty. Seasonal rental dates by application; exact winter availability unknown. Apply through the town; resident reservations open the first business day in January for the next two seasons with $250 deposit, non-residents for the upcoming season with $400 deposit; final rental fee unknown.

items.b: A state fisheries site provides a fishing dock and views over rocky coves. Public access point; use the linked map and obey current signs. Use the official timetable and trip planner; some trips and connections vary by day, so do not assume every listed run serves Jamestown.
Children in grades 3–5 discuss Rhode Island Children’s Book Award nominees. Posted Wednesdays 3:45–4:30 PM. Pick up the selection at Youth Services, read as much as possible and attend.
Writers of all experience levels share memories and develop personal stories. Mondays 10:30–11:30 AM. Beginners are welcome to attend the listed workshop.

items.n: Safe Harbor Jamestown Boatyard private beach
items.b: The boatyard offers a small private beach among its boating-customer amenities. By customer arrangement; beach hours unknown. Reserve a berth or mooring and ask about beach eligibility; public beach admission, lifeguards and restroom access unknown; 2026 transient moorings start at $90/night for smaller boats.

The parish music ministry contributes to Catholic worship on the island. Choir rehearsal unknown; Mass Saturday 4:00 PM and Sunday 8:00 and 10:30 AM. Contact the parish office to ask about joining the music ministry.

Episcopal parish hosting worship, community music and a thrift shop. Sunday worship 8:00 AM and 10:00 AM; Wednesday morning prayer and Bible study 10:00 AM; thrift shop Saturday 9:00 AM–noon. Hosts Community Piano concerts, usually Sunday 2:00 PM; specific winter dates unconfirmed.

items.n: Saint Matthew’s Church Choir and Music Ministry
items.b: A church choir contributes to worship in a parish that also hosts community concerts. Choir rehearsal Thursdays 7:00 PM; Sunday worship 8:00 and 10:00 AM. Contact the parish office about singing; public worship welcomes visitors.

items.n: Saint Matthew’s community crafts and bingo
items.b: The parish calendar lists recurring craft and bingo gatherings. Got Crafts fourth Tuesday 1:30 PM; bingo Friday 1:00 PM. Contact the parish for visitor arrangements and any participation charges.

An organized bay swim raises funds for coastal conservation and finishes in Jamestown. Annual summer event; no winter swim date verified. Register as a swimmer or use the organizer’s volunteer signup when available.

Local Scout troop offering outdoor education, service and community volunteering. Dated troop calendar lists Thursday meetings 7:00–8:00 PM at Lawn Avenue School; older homepage text names the former senior-center location. Community service includes December holiday luminaries. Youth meetings and outings are not listed in Part B.
An older town license identifies a snack-bar operation at Dutch Harbor. Ask the boatyard whether food service currently operates; reservations and seasonal closure unknown.
nt: Hours and details not recently confirmed; check before visiting.

items.b: Save The Bay offers winter boat trips to observe seals around the lower bay. Published season November–April; individual times vary with the booking calendar. Reserve through the official ticket link; one-hour tour $25 standard or $20 qualifying discounted rate, under-three children no charge; travel to Newport first.
nt: Hours and details not recently confirmed; check before visiting.

Experienced players gather for mah-jongg. Tuesdays 2:30 PM. Contact Senior Services; the advertised session is for experienced players.
Older adults take a dance-based movement class. Mondays 10:00–10:45 AM. Drop in; advertised fee is $5 per class.

Restrooms: Available according to shoreline guide; winter opening unknown. Lifeguards: unknown.

Use the town’s permit portal and licensed-property records; state registration also applies to stays of 30 nights or fewer advertised through a third-party platform; verify occupancy, inspection and local-representative requirements with the town.

Use the official takeout link https://snackbarroyale.square.site or inquire through the site; reservations and winter closure unknown.
This library reading program was advertised for children in grades 3 and 4. Current schedule unknown. Ask Youth Services about the current program and registration.

Public coastal viewpoints provide westward sunsets and harbor or lighthouse scenes. Park or access-point hours apply; exact sunset time varies by date. Use established public paths and the individual parking instructions; Spirketing faces the West Passage while Fort Wetherill overlooks Newport Harbor.

items.n: Tall Tailz — fishing and sightseeing charters
items.b: A charter operator offers fishing and custom sightseeing trips from Clark Boat Yard. By reservation; operator describes its usual fishing season as late April–late November. Contact the captain for a trip, price, departure time and weather decision; winter departures unknown.
nt: Hours and details not recently confirmed; check before visiting.

items.b: Volunteer group restoring native habitat and caring for Taylor Point. Volunteer restoration work parties; dates and times announced separately.
Students in grades 9–12 advise the library and undertake volunteer projects. Posted monthly Tuesdays 4:00–4:30 PM. Contact Colleen LeBeau to participate and commit to meeting dates.

The public golf course’s snack bar welcomes golfers and other visitors. Daily opening 8:00 AM; closing time unknown; operator posts November 30 seasonal closure. Visit without playing golf or call about group outings; next spring reopening unknown.

Jamestown Primary Care is part of Brown University Health and provides family-medicine services on Southwest Avenue. The practice supports routine preventive care and ongoing health needs, with sick visits arranged by appointment. Its current system affiliation and practice name are useful when locating the correct office or patient information online.
nt: Use the office phone or patient portal for appointments; no public general email verified.

items.b: Jamestown Real Estate works with property in Jamestown, South County and Aquidneck Island. Its village office supplies a direct local contact for buying, selling and questions about current listings. The company's website provides property-search tools, helping clients begin a search before discussing the details with an agent.

Jamestown Wine & Spirits stocks beer, wine and spirits on Southwest Avenue. Alongside beverages, its Chamber listing notes Jamestown souvenirs, lottery sales and food items to take away. The business also maintains an online catalog, providing a way to browse products before visiting the shop.

JB's on the Water occupies a waterfront setting at the Bay Voyage property, overlooking Narragansett Bay and the Newport Bridge. The restaurant offers indoor dining, seasonal outdoor seating and weekend brunch. Its location is a distinguishing feature, with the water and bridge forming the backdrop to a meal.

Ken's Barber Shop provides barber services for adults and children on Conanicus Avenue. It is a straightforward local option for routine haircuts within the village. The business maintains a public social page under the Bestview name; call the shop to confirm current appointment or walk-in arrangements.

Latitude supplies and personalizes clothing and accessories for yachts, teams, events and individual customers. The company describes more than 35 years in crew gear, including technical and foul-weather clothing. Monogramming and custom decoration extend its work beyond sailing uniforms to everyday apparel and gifts.
nt: Contact for custom orders and visiting arrangements.

items.b: Lila Delman Compass maintains a Jamestown real-estate office on Narragansett Avenue. The firm handles sales and rentals, with its local profile emphasizing luxury and waterfront property. It also operates offices elsewhere in Rhode Island, connecting its island practice with a wider regional property network.
nt: Email reaches the firm's general contact.

items.b: Lionel Champlin Guest House is a historic Victorian inn on Lincoln Street, offering rooms with private bathrooms and an apartment option. Its website describes more than 20 years of hosting visitors. The setting suits travelers looking for a smaller village lodging property with convenient access to Jamestown and nearby Newport.

items.a: Bomes Theater Offices 34 Narragansett Avenue, Suite 1
items.b: Lisa Carlisle Architect specializes in residential architecture, including classic shingle-style homes and New England seaside design with modern elements. The office is in the Bomes Theater building on Narragansett Avenue. Its portfolio encompasses custom homes and renovations, with design shaped around the property and the household's requirements.

Mark E. Liberati Law Offices appears among the Jamestown Community Chorus's published local business supporters, with a Narragansett Avenue office and direct telephone number. That source establishes a community-facing professional contact. Call the office to confirm its current practice areas and whether it can assist with a particular matter.
nt: Directory-based contact; services and current operation should be confirmed.

The Jamestown location is part of a small regional operation that also has stores in Westerly and Mystic. It serves both everyday household shopping and boating provisions.

Milo's Nails & Spa is publicly listed as a nail salon on Narragansett Avenue, with manicures, pedicures and nail styling among the described services. It adds a personal-care option within the village center. Call to confirm the current service menu, booking arrangements and business details before making a visit.
nt: Directory-based listing; current operation not independently confirmed.

nt: Published business address; contact before visiting.

Its published contact details provide direct access to the local attorneys, with information available through the firm's website. Prospective clients should discuss the particular matter with the office to establish the appropriate services and representation.

The Narragansett Cafe combines a neighborhood restaurant and bar with live entertainment. Located on Narragansett Avenue, it is a place to check for local music as well as food and drinks. Performers and show times change, so its current entertainment calendar is the useful starting point for planning a visit.

Nauti Girl Boutique is a woman-owned coastal shop carrying clothing, shoes, accessories, gifts and beach-inspired decor. Its Jamestown location is on Conanicus Avenue, with another location in Narragansett. The selection is organized around coastal living, making it relevant to both island residents and visitors shopping for vacation wear.

Our Table Jamestown serves a seasonal, scratch-made dinner menu under executive chefs Marc Alexander and Marla Romash. The chefs divide their attention between savory cooking and desserts, a useful detail behind the restaurant's menu. The business operates year-round and offers outdoor seating when conditions allow.

items.n: Out of the Box Studio & Gallery
items.b: Out of the Box Studio & Gallery offers exhibitions, studio space and creative support in an inclusive environment. Its community includes artists with and without disabilities, as well as people developing their artistic practice. The Clinton Avenue gallery also provides opportunities for visitors to see and purchase artwork.

Pinheiro Construction works on custom homes, renovations and historic restoration. Its published capabilities also include decks and millwork, allowing a project to range from a specific building detail to a larger residential transformation. The company's Jamestown contact provides a starting point for reviewing the property, design and intended scope.

The Purple Door is an art and jewelry business on Conanicus Avenue, also identified through its public Facebook page as the Purple Door Bead Shop. It adds a small specialty-shopping stop to the waterfront end of the village. Contact the shop directly for current stock, custom work and opening arrangements.

R.A.M. Construction handles excavation and masonry, including foundations, site work, septic systems, pavers, walkways, terraces and driveways. Its Chamber profile recounts a beginning with a small dump truck and an assortment of small jobs. The company continues to describe work ranging from minor repairs to larger construction projects.
nt: Published business address; contact before visiting.

The firm describes a full-service approach to local property transactions. Its office is a resource for discussing listings and market activity, with advice tailored to a specific property or search.

Ribbit Wellness offers yoga, meditation, wellness coaching and workshops from its North Road location. Its range combines movement-based classes with opportunities for reflection and individual support. Programs and schedules vary, so the studio's own calendar and direct contact are the best starting points for selecting a session.

S. Barzin Architect is Shahin Barzin's architecture practice, working on residential and commercial projects. His background includes architecture and interior-architecture study at the Rhode Island School of Design. The practice discusses technology and sustainable design alongside the character of the building, connecting technical planning with the way a space is experienced.
nt: Published practice address; arrange appointments in advance.

items.b: The Secret Garden combines a florist with a garden center on Southwest Avenue. Services and products range from arrangements for celebrations and memorial occasions to plants, gardening supplies and seasonal decorations. Its year-round identity changes with the season, from spring planting to autumn displays and holiday greenery.

Slice of Heaven is a village bakery, cafe and restaurant serving breakfast, lunch and baked goods. Its offerings also include seasonal treats and beverages, with the cafe functioning as both a quick stop and a place to sit down. The Narragansett Avenue address places it among the village's shops and restaurants.

Standards serves homestyle dishes and traditional family favorites at 40 Narragansett Avenue. Draft beer, wine and cocktails accompany the food. The restaurant's name reflects its focus on familiar meals, making its own current menu the best guide to the dishes and specials available on a particular visit.

Stephen Dargo's architectural practice publishes a Jamestown address and direct professional contact details. His portfolio and professional résumé provide the starting point for learning about past design work and discussing a potential commission. Contact the practice to confirm its current project availability and the arrangements for a consultation.
nt: Contact details are from a published 2024 professional résumé; reconfirm before publication.

items.b: Sunset Beach Oyster Bar links a Jamestown shellfish business with an oyster-bar setting on Narragansett Avenue. Its published business description identifies both shellfish farming and oyster service, giving the operation a direct connection to local aquaculture. Contact the business for current opening arrangements and oyster availability.

Susan Hackman, CPA, offers tax planning and preparation for individuals, businesses and trusts. Her published practice description also includes small-business accounting, consulting and QuickBooks experience. The combination serves clients who need continuing bookkeeping or business support as well as assistance at tax-filing time.
nt: Published business address; arrange appointments in advance.

items.b: A seasonal ice-cream shop offers scoops, shakes and desserts. Published season early May–October; November–March hours unknown. Contact the shop for its next opening and any off-season orders.

TMT Construction is publicly listed as a Jamestown residential contractor associated with Thomas Tiernan. Its Buoy Street business listing supplies a local point of contact for construction inquiries. Detailed company history and current project scope were not established from a primary website, so prospective customers should confirm these directly.
nt: Directory-based listing; current operation not independently confirmed.

items.b: Tollgate Orthodontics operates a Jamestown location on Clinton Avenue in addition to its Warwick office. Its services include braces and clear-aligner treatment. A distinctive offering is the practice's own True brand of aligners; contact the office to discuss suitability, appointment locations and the current treatment options.

Town organizer and publisher of community programs, celebrations and public information. Community events listed at https://www.jamestownri.gov/news; tree lighting and seasonal activities are announced individually. Government and election meetings are excluded from Part B.

Conanicut Marina provides dockage and moorings at East Ferry. Its published profile describes more than 4,500 linear feet of dockage, capacity for vessels up to 225 feet and 150 moorings. The marina's village location places boaters near shops, restaurants and ferry connections.

Dutch Harbor Boat Yard is a full-service yard and mooring facility on Jamestown's west side. It offers boat storage and maintenance, with services supporting both the boating season and winter layup. Its location places it in a different harbor setting from the marinas and ferry facilities at East Ferry.

Taylor Point Boat Yard handles repair, maintenance, hauling, launching and storage for recreational and commercial vessels. The facility also lists Yamaha outboard sales and service. Its combination of indoor and outdoor storage with mechanical support makes it a year-round marine service location rather than solely a summer docking facility.

items.n: Trocki Paquin Attorneys and Counsellors at Law
items.b: Trocki Paquin Attorneys and Counsellors at Law offers legal representation and mediation. Its practice areas include divorce and family matters, estate planning and probate, business and employment issues, landlord-tenant matters and personal injury. Attorneys Kristine Trocki and Monique Paquin Duarte identify communication and conflict resolution as central to their approach.
The library presents afternoon film screenings. Posted Tuesdays 1:30 PM; listed through January 2027. Contact the library or consult the event page before attending.

TWC Home combines a shop with interior and landscape design services. Owners Deb and Toby present home furnishings and gifts alongside a garden setting at the Narragansett Avenue property. Visitors can browse the retail selection while also asking about larger projects for a room, home or outdoor space.

Public parking areas serve the village and East Ferry departures. All-day spaces identified by ferry operator; individual posted limits apply. Use the operator’s map: 11 Knowles Court, seaward spaces between 9 and 30 Conanicus Avenue, and spaces between 60 and 99 Narragansett Avenue; paid or overnight ferry parking is advertised May–October; winter fees unknown.

Village Hearth makes pastries, breads and cafe food from scratch, with sandwiches, soups and other offerings changing with the season. Owners Stephanie and Lindsay Haigh moved from Atlanta to Jamestown in December 2020 before taking on the bakery. The business brings a neighborhood cafe setting to Watson Avenue.

Working heritage farm offering public tours and educational activities. Self-guided tours Thursday and Saturday 1:00–4:00 PM, June–mid-October; seasonal farm workshops and special events. No winter event dates confirmed.

Wellworks is a Jamestown well and water-system business listed in the National Ground Water Association's contractor directory. Its public service descriptions cover well pumps and related water equipment. Contact the company with the property location and the type of water-system question to establish the appropriate visit or service.

items.a: At the west end of Narragansett Avenue, Jamestown, RI
items.b: A public waterfront overlook and pier face Dutch Harbor and the West Passage. Public access point; use the linked map and obey current signs. Guide lists no charge for access; parking conditions below are separate. Parking: Pier parking listed; current limits unknown. Restrooms: Available according to shoreline guide; winter opening unknown. Lifeguards: unknown. Southern pier facilities require the relevant town permit; public shoreline access does not grant permission to use every dock.
nt: Hours and details not recently confirmed; check before visiting.

items.b: Wildflower Farm grows seasonal flowers and offers bouquets, subscriptions and floral products from its Jamestown property. Its farm stand and online ordering connect customers directly with the grower, with local pickup and delivery options described on its website. Workshops and flower availability vary with the growing season.
nt: Seasonal farm stand; confirm visiting and pickup arrangements.

items.b: Windmist Farm is a family-run operation producing pasture-raised meats, eggs and seasonal vegetables. Customers can visit the farm shop and see its working agricultural setting on Weeden Lane. The farm's land-preservation story is documented by USDA, linking local food production with efforts to retain agricultural land on Conanicut Island.
nt: Farm website announces a seasonal store closing on November 1, 2026.

items.b: Wolpert Insurance & Risk Management's Chamber profile lists a Jamestown business contact for insurance services, including personal, commercial and marine coverage. The company website now directs visitors into World Insurance's organization. Contact the listed representative to confirm the appropriate office and arrange a discussion of current insurance services.
nt: Chamber-listed Jamestown contact; arrange appointments before visiting.
Nonprofit and community listings are separate from the 98 business entries.
